about.title: Dinuba Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Dinuba's roads carry a steady mix of local traffic and agricultural routes, and corridors like Avenue 416, Alta Avenue, and El Monte Way see their share of crashes, with Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m. a common time for collisions to occur. Tulare County's public crash records show dozens of injury collisions here each year, and behind every number is someone dealing with medical bills, missed work, and a damaged vehicle. Our team helps injured Dinuba residents get the legal representation they need at no upfront cost. We handle personal injury claims and can evaluate what happened and explain your options. You won't have to sort through insurance calls and paperwork alone while you're still recovering. The sooner you have someone in your corner, the better positioned you'll be to protect your claim.
commonInjuries: Cuts, bruising, and soft tissue trauma

whyChoose.title: Why Act Quickly After a Dinuba Crash

items.title: California's Filing Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but that window shrinks dramatically — sometimes to just six months — if a government entity like a city or county was involved. Waiting to seek legal advice can quietly cost you your right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work For You
items.desc: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still pursue compensation even if you're partly to blame for the crash, though your recovery gets reduced by your share of fault. Our team can help make sure fault isn't unfairly pinned on you before you've had a chance to explain your side.

items.title: Don't Let the Insurer Get Ahead of You
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often call quickly after a crash asking for a recorded statement — and anything you say can be used to downplay your claim later. Preserving evidence early and speaking with our team before giving a statement helps protect the value of your case.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Dinuba?
items.answer: Under California law, you typically have two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your accident involved a government vehicle or a hazard on a public road, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth getting advice sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if the accident happened on Avenue 416 or another busy Dinuba road?
items.answer: Corridors like Avenue 416, Alta Avenue, and El Monte Way see a notable share of Dinuba's reported collisions, and the specific circumstances — traffic signals, turning lanes, visibility — can matter a lot for a claim. Our team can look at the location details and any available records to help piece together what happened.

items.question: Will I owe anything upfront to speak with an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our initial consultation is free, and we typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after you contact us.
